For the basic garden veggies, I'd suggest regular seed starting mix. https://www.lowes.com/pd/Miracle-Gro-8-Dry-Quart-Seed-Starting-Mix/1000067923?cm_mmc=SCE_PLA--LawnGarden--Soil-_-1000067923:Miracle-Gro&CAWELAID=&kpid=1000067923&CAGPSPN=pla&store_code=2607&k_clickID=c69697ad-ef50-44b4-a27a-9551197431f1&gclid=CjwKCAjw4sLVBRAlEiwASblR-zF9UY-peG9thf0eSEJU7kV8oLnZoxR3oxmsqQhsmKetgJmHamTNyhoCT4kQAvD_BwE

Fill up the trays/flats/cups half way with it and pack it down well. Get it good and soaked and let any excess drain out for a few minutes. Use dry mix on top of that to the level you want and make sure its pretty well packed down. I use another flat or cup to just press everything down a bit, otherwise the moisture will cause the mix to settle in the bottom. Put the seeds on top of this to whatever depth they need to be planted, then top off with more dry mix. I'll usually put a few drops of water on top of this, but only a little bit. Make sure the soil is to the top of the container, otherwise your seedlings will be reaching for light. Then put the container in a clear sealed box or cover in plastic wrap until the seeds emerge. The moisture from the bottom half will moisten the soil on the top and you should be good with watering for at least a week. They really don't need much water at all.
